audits.title: P24 Auditing antibiotic course lengths for the management of community-acquired pneumonia and hospital-acquired pneumonia against current NICE guidance
audits.standard: NICE guidance to stop antibiotics at day 5 for CAP/HAP if clinically stable
audits.setting: Medical specialties, RCHT (Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 10 (45%) received 5 or 6 days; 12 (55%) received 7 to 10 days despite meeting stop criteria; mean 6.5 and median 6.3 days

audits.other_findings: Education and an EPMA day-5 alert are proposed; re-audit with a larger sample recommended.
audits.citation: . P24 Auditing antibiotic course lengths for the management of community-acquired pneumonia and hospital-acquired pneumonia against current NICE guidance. JAC Antimicrob Resist. 2023;5(Suppl 2).

audits.title: Audit of the use of erythromycin in the treatment of community-acquired lower respiratory infections.
audits.standard: British Thoracic Society community-acquired pneumonia guidelines (beta-lactam first, erythromycin added for atypical features)
audits.setting: Sandwell District General Hospital, West Midlands

cycle1.result: Erythromycin continuation justified in 10 (16%); prescribed and continued unnecessarily in 47/62.

audits.other_findings: Five patients were severe enough to justify combined therapy.

audits.title: [Management of acute community-acquired pneumonia in a health centre. Assessment of 101 cases using the retrospective clinical audit method].
audits.setting: French university hospital, CHU de Grenoble

cycle1.result: Appropriate level of care in 40; appropriate microbiology in 18; antibiotics within 8 hours in 43; appropriate empirical antibiotics in 38.

audits.other_findings: In-hospital mortality 14; compliance was not linked to mortality.

audits.title: A quality improvement initiative to improve adherence to national guidelines for empiric management of community-acquired pneumonia in emergency departments.
audits.standard: Australian national guidelines for empiric community-acquired pneumonia management; documented pneumonia severity index use and concordant antibiotic prescribing
audits.setting: 37 emergency departments (public, private, rural and metropolitan), 26 completing

cycle1.result: Documented PSI use 30/518 (6%, 95% CI 4-8); practice varied and mostly discordant with guidelines.

audits.intervention: Drug use evaluation with academic detailing, group feedback presentations and prescribing prompts, in two intervention phases.
audits.other_findings: Three audits of 20 consecutive presentations per hospital; antibiotic concordance result truncated in abstract.
audits.citation: McIntosh KA, Maxwell DJ, Pulver LK, Horn F, Robertson MB, Kaye KI, et al.. A quality improvement initiative to improve adherence to national guidelines for empiric management of community-acquired pneumonia in emergency departments. audits.title: British Thoracic Society adult community acquired pneumonia audit 2009/10.
audits.standard: BTS Guidelines for the management of community acquired pneumonia in adults (2009) and local CAP guidelines

cycle1.result: Initial empirical antibiotics in accordance with local guidelines in 1478 (55.5%); chest x-ray within 4 hours in 83% and first antibiotic dose within 4 hours in 58%.

audits.other_findings: 30-day in-hospital mortality 503 (18.3%); IV antibiotics given in 65%, 74% and 90% of CURB65 0-1, 2 and 3-5 patients.
audits.citation: Lim WS, Woodhead M, British Thoracic Society. British Thoracic Society adult community acquired pneumonia audit 2009/10. Thorax. 2011;66(6):548-549. doi:10.1136/thoraxjnl-2011-200081. PMID: 21502103.

audits.title: Audit of physicians' adherence to a preprinted order set for community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.standard: Institutional preprinted order set for community-acquired pneumonia; IDSA-ATS guidelines
audits.setting: University Hospital of Northern British Columbia, Prince George

cycle1.result: Preprinted order used for 25/58 (43%); all sections used correctly in 4 (7%).

audits.other_findings: Order set use increased guideline-concordant therapy (p=0.012), vaccination assessment (25% v 9%) and PSI use (52% v 0%).

audits.title: An audit of inpatient management of community-acquired pneumonia in Oman: a comparison with regional clinical guidelines.

cycle1.result: CURB-65 documented in 4 (2.3%); smoking history 56 (32.6%); standard co-amoxiclav and clarithromycin in 115 (67%); antibiotics within 4 hours in 139 (81%).

audits.other_findings: No documented offer of influenza or pneumococcal vaccine; clinical coding of CAP poor.

audits.title: Mortality reduction in adult community-acquired pneumonia in the UK (2009-2014): results from the British Thoracic Society audit programme.
audits.setting: UK hospitals (British Thoracic Society national CAP audit)

cycle1.result: 30-day inpatient mortality fell over 6 years (2014 vs 2009 adjusted OR 0.86; p for trend 0.004); chest X-ray and first antibiotic within 4 hours of admission increased by 3.7% and 11.5%.

audits.other_findings: Authors expect further gains from the 2016 NICE pneumonia quality standard.
audits.citation: Daniel P, Woodhead M, Welham S, Mckeever TM, Lim WS, British Thoracic Society. Mortality reduction in adult community-acquired pneumonia in the UK (2009-2014): results from the British Thoracic Society audit programme. Thorax. 2016;71(11):1061-1063. doi:10.1136/thoraxjnl-2016-208937. PMID: 27534681.

audits.standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines for empiric CAP treatment based on CURB-65

cycle1.result: Guideline-concordant empiric antibiotics in 48% of cases; 100% concordance when CURB-65 was documented.

audits.other_findings: Excessively broad-spectrum and inappropriate antibiotic use was a notable problem.

audits.standard: NICE and American Thoracic Society guidelines for community-acquired pneumonia

cycle1.result: CURB-65 determined for 12 (12%); urea not documented in 48 (48%); respiratory rate not documented in 73 (73%); microbiology in 2 (2%); 81 (81%) received β-lactam plus macrolide.

audits.title: Audit of a multidisciplinary approach to improve management of community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.standard: Standards of care for CAP including CURB65 documentation and empirical antibiotic prescribing guidelines
audits.setting: James Paget University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: CURB65 score documented in 32/62; chest X-ray findings documented in 59/62; 85.5% compliant with antibiotic prescribing guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Authors state the multidisciplinary approach considerably improved compliance with most standards, but no earlier figures are given in the abstract.

audits.title: An audit of community-acquired pneumonia antimicrobial compliance using an intervention bundle in an Irish hospital.
audits.standard: Local CAP antimicrobial guidelines in keeping with British Thoracic Society CAP guidelines

cycle1.result: Overall compliance with local CAP guidelines 21.6%.

audits.intervention: Intervention bundle: mobile audience response system, promotion of antimicrobial app, physical card with local guidelines, CURB-65 incorporated into the unscheduled admission proforma.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance with local CAP guidelines 62.5%.

audits.other_findings: Total antibiotic duration was shortened; secondary measures included length of stay, mortality and CURB-65 documentation.
audits.citation: O'Kelly B, Rueda-Benito A, O'Regan M, Finan K. An audit of community-acquired pneumonia antimicrobial compliance using an intervention bundle in an Irish hospital. J Glob Antimicrob Resist. 2020;23:38-45. doi:10.1016/j.jgar.2020.07.021. PMID: 32801028.

audits.title: Diagnosis and Therapy of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Observational Study and Medical Audit.
audits.setting: Swiss general hospital medical wards (Cantonal Hospital Baselland)

cycle1.result: Respiratory rate documentation missing in 23%; procalcitonin 23.2%; urinary antigen testing about 90%; blood cultures about 80%; arterial blood gas 39%; guideline-adherent empiric antibiotics 75%; ceftriaxone use 19.7%; mean antibiotic duration 8.2 days vs 5-7 days recommended.

audits.other_findings: Oral steroids given to 29.1% of patients, including 75% of those with COPD; twelve different antibiotic regimens used.
audits.citation: Lüthi-Corridori G, Roth AI, Boesing M, Jaun F, Tarr PE, Leuppi-Taegtmeyer AB, et al.. Diagnosis and Therapy of Community-Acquired Pneumonia in the Emergency Department: A Retrospective Observational Study and Medical Audit. J Clin Med. 2024;13(2):574. doi:10.3390/jcm13020574. PMID: 38276080.

audits.standard: NICE NG250: CURB-65 documented in all adults with CAP (100%)

audits.title: A criterion based audit of community-acquired pneumonia.
audits.standard: Complete objective severity assessment and microbiological testing on admission (criterion-based)
audits.setting: Specialist respiratory unit, West Norwich Hospital

cycle1.result: Standard of initial assessment was high; seven markers of severity recorded consistently.

audits.intervention: Rubber stamp with a checklist of microbiological investigations in the notes

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in thoroughness of microbiological investigations.

audits.other_findings: 48 patients across both periods; two or more markers of severity helped predict outcome.
audits.citation: May HM, Harrison TS, Harrison BD. A criterion based audit of community-acquired pneumonia. Respir Med. 1994;88(9):693-696. doi:10.1016/s0954-6111(05)80069-1. PMID: 7809443.

audits.title: An audit of the assessment and management of adults admitted to Christchurch Hospital with community acquired pneumonia.
audits.standard: Management guidelines and modified British Thoracic Society severity criteria

cycle1.result: Guidelines followed without exception in 15%; only 33% of severe cases correctly identified; 71% of severe cases given one antibiotic; first dose delayed in 44%.

audits.other_findings: Follow-up chest radiograph in 43 (51%) of those discharged; further education recommended.
audits.citation: Meyer RJ, Town GI, Harrè E, Koning M, Hurrell M, Beard ME, et al.. An audit of the assessment and management of adults admitted to Christchurch Hospital with community acquired pneumonia. N Z Med J. 1997;110(1052):349-352. PMID: 9364175.
